bug_description.normalized: When `file` classifies the 10-byte witness `yyprevious` as text, `file_ascmagic_with_encoding` allocates a UTF-8 buffer sized as `ulen * 6`, so the 60-byte heap allocation contains uninitialized tail bytes beyond the encoded 10-byte ASCII prefix. In the text soft-magic pass, the top-level lex rule from `magic/Magdir/lex:7` (`0 search/100 yyprevious`) matches and sets `ms->search.rm_len` to 10. Its continuation from `magic/Magdir/lex:8` (`>3 search/1 >\0  for %s`) then retargets `ms->search.s` to `utf8_buf + 3` and `ms->search.s_len` to 7 but leaves `rm_len` unchanged. The vulnerable FILE_SEARCH loop compares the current byte `'r'` against `\0`, exhausts the one-byte search range without finding the terminator, and falls out instead of returning 0. The subsequent `>` relation therefore treats the failed continuation search as matched, `match()` reaches the print path, and `mprint()` calls `strndup(ms->search.s, ms->search.rm_len)` with `ms->search.s = utf8_buf + 3` and stale `rm_len = 10`. That probes past the 7 initialized bytes remaining in the current window into the uninitialized tail of `utf8_buf`, and MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at `mprint` line 675.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing text path that consumes the attacker-controlled bytes and materializes decoded text state `ubuf/ulen` for the later UTF-8 conversion and soft-magic search logic.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is the exact 10-byte ASCII string `yyprevious`. On the observed path, `file_encoding` treats those bytes as text and returns `ulen = 10`, which is then used to size and populate the UTF-8 buffer searched by the lex rules.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `mprint` duplicates the current search pointer with a stale length, so the continuation print path reads past the initialized suffix of `utf8_buf` into heap bytes that were never written.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor___strndup at offset 7 inside [0x704000000003, 8)` and attributes the poisoned bytes to the `malloc` at `file_ascmagic_with_encoding` line 136.

root_cause.code: for (idx = 0; m->str_range == 0 || idx < m->str_range; idx++) { if (slen + idx > ms->search.s_len) return 0; v = file_strncmp(m->value.s, ms->search.s + idx, slen, m->str_flags); if (v == 0) { ms->search.offset += idx; ms->search.rm_len = ms->search.s_len - idx; break; } }
root_cause.description: Root cause. The FILE_SEARCH miss path does not return 0 when a range-limited search exhausts `m->str_range` without a match, so the last nonzero comparison result survives and stale `ms->search.rm_len` stays live for later printing.
root_cause.note: On the lex continuation `>3 search/1 >\0  for %s`, the only comparison is against the byte `'r'` at offset 3, so `v` becomes positive. Because the one-byte range ends immediately afterward, control falls out of the loop instead of rejecting the rule. The later `>` relation then interprets that positive `v` as a successful match and reaches `mprint` with `rm_len` still taken from the earlier top-level lex match.

parser_admitted.code: if ((rv = file_softmagic(ms, utf8_buf, (size_t)(utf8_end - utf8_buf), NULL, NULL, TEXTTEST, text)) == 0)
parser_admitted.description: After text decoding, the witness enters the TEXTTEST soft-magic engine on the UTF-8 buffer. On this path, the lex rules from `magic/Magdir/lex:7-8` are evaluated against the attacker-controlled string.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized bytes consumed at the sink come from the heap allocation of `utf8_buf`. `encode_utf8` writes only the prefix up to `utf8_end`; the remaining tail bytes in this allocation stay indeterminate and are what MSAN traces back to this `malloc`.

fine_trace.code: if (file_encoding(ms, buf, nbytes, &ubuf, &ulen, &code, &code_mime, &type) == 0) rv = 0; else rv = file_ascmagic_with_encoding(ms, buf, nbytes, ubuf, ulen, code, type, text);
fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled bytes `yyprevious` on the text path and materializes decoded text state `ubuf/ulen`. For this ASCII witness, `ulen` is 10 and drives the later UTF-8 allocation and searches.

fine_trace.code: mlen = ulen * 6; if ((utf8_buf = CAST(unsigned char *, malloc(mlen))) == NULL) {
fine_trace.note: Derives the UTF-8 heap-buffer size from attacker-controlled `ulen` and allocates `utf8_buf`. MSAN's origin report points to this allocation because its tail bytes are uninitialized until explicitly written.

fine_trace.code: if ((utf8_end = encode_utf8(utf8_buf, mlen, ubuf, ulen)) == NULL) goto done; if ((rv = file_softmagic(ms, utf8_buf, (size_t)(utf8_end - utf8_buf), NULL, NULL, TEXTTEST, text)) == 0) rv = -1;
fine_trace.note: Encodes the witness into `utf8_buf` and immediately passes only the initialized prefix length `utf8_end - utf8_buf` into text soft-magic. For the ASCII witness, the prefix is 10 bytes (`yyprevious`), so the remaining heap tail from step 2 stays uninitialized.

fine_trace.code: ms->search.s = RCAST(const char *, s) + offset; ms->search.s_len = nbytes - offset; ms->search.offset = offset;
fine_trace.note: For the top-level lex rule from `magic/Magdir/lex:7` (`0 search/100 yyprevious`), `offset` is 0, so `mcopy` materializes a search window over the entire 10-byte UTF-8 buffer.

fine_trace.code: v = file_strncmp(m->value.s, ms->search.s + idx, slen, m->str_flags); if (v == 0) { ms->search.offset += idx; ms->search.rm_len = ms->search.s_len - idx; break; }
fine_trace.note: The top-level lex rule's search string is exactly `yyprevious`, so the first comparison succeeds at `idx == 0` and stores `ms->search.rm_len = 10`. That shared length later becomes stale state for the continuation.

fine_trace.code: ms->search.s = RCAST(const char *, s) + offset; ms->search.s_len = nbytes - offset; ms->search.offset = offset;
fine_trace.note: The continuation rule from `magic/Magdir/lex:8` (`>3 search/1 >\0  for %s`) retargets the search window to `utf8_buf + 3`, so `ms->search.s_len` becomes 7 and `ms->search.offset` becomes 3. This FILE_SEARCH `mcopy` arm does not reset `ms->search.rm_len`, so the value 10 from step 5 remains live.

fine_trace.code: for (idx = 0; m->str_range == 0 || idx < m->str_range; idx++) { if (slen + idx > ms->search.s_len) return 0; v = file_strncmp(m->value.s, ms->search.s + idx, slen, m->str_flags); if (v == 0) { ms->search.offset += idx; ms->search.rm_len = ms->search.s_len - idx; break; } }
fine_trace.note: Root cause. For the continuation `>3 search/1 >\0  for %s`, `m->str_range` is 1 and `m->value.s` is `\0`. The only comparison is against the byte `'r'` at `utf8_buf[3]`, so `v` becomes positive. Because the allowed range is exhausted immediately afterward, this vulnerable loop falls out instead of returning 0, leaving the failed-search comparison result and the stale `rm_len = 10` from step 5 intact.

fine_trace.code: case '>': if (m->flag & UNSIGNED) { matched = v > l; } else { matched = (int64_t)v > (int64_t)l; }
fine_trace.note: FILE_SEARCH leaves `l = 0`, and the lex continuation's relation is `>`, parsed from the leading `>` in `magic/Magdir/lex:8`. The positive `v` from step 7 therefore makes `matched` nonzero even though the one-byte search never found `\0`.
The continuation takes the nonzero `magiccheck` branch instead of `case 0`, so `match()` continues into the print path for the lex continuation whose description is `for %s`.

Sink. `ms->search.s` now points at `utf8_buf + 3`, where only 7 initialized bytes remain, but `ms->search.rm_len` is still 10 from step 5. `strndup` therefore probes past the initialized suffix into the uninitialized heap tail created at step 2 and only partially filled at step 3, which is exactly what the saved MSAN trace reports.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The fix commit's `FILE_SEARCH` change enforces the missing obligation this trace exposes: when a search does not find its needle within the permitted range, it must return 0 instead of falling through to the relation check and later print path.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partial — MSAN's origin frame identifies the uninitialized heap bytes in `utf8_buf`, but the project bug is the later FILE_SEARCH miss path that reuses stale `rm_len` and lets a failed continuation search reach `mprint`.

format.name: Exact 10-byte ASCII witness for the lex search continuation
format.contract: The available runtime evidence proves the exact staged witness only: the 10-byte ASCII string `yyprevious`. Its trigger semantics are specific to the lex rules in `magic/Magdir/lex:7-8`: the top-level `search/100 yyprevious` rule must match first so `ms->search.rm_len` becomes 10, and the continuation `>3 search/1 >\0  for %s` must then examine offset 3 where the witness byte is `'r'` and no `\0` exists within the one-byte search range. That leaves a positive FILE_SEARCH comparison result and stale `rm_len`, so `mprint` reaches `strndup(ms->search.s, ms->search.rm_len)` with `ms->search.s = utf8_buf + 3` and reads into the uninitialized heap tail. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader input class beyond this exact witness and these rule properties.
